Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex EV Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. Today's conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex EV's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Javier Ramirez, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Mike Thompson, Chief Manufacturing Officer; and Dr. Lena Novak, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Javier Ramirez.

Javier Ramirez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 was a significant quarter for Apex EV, marked by progress across our key strategic initiatives. We achieved notable milestones in explosive software and services revenue growth, robust production volume increases and capacity utilization improvements, resilient average selling price trends across models and regions, strong delivery volume guidance by model, expanding gross margins per vehicle, and substantial changes in our order backlog and reservation trends showing continued strength. We are particularly pleased with the initial customer response to our new Zephyr SUV platform, and its positive impact on our backlog is substantial, driving us toward sustained profitability.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Javier. Good morning, everyone. For Q3, our revenue reached $7.2 billion, demonstrating a 45% increase compared to the same period last year. Our gross margin stood at 25%, reflecting our commitment to operational excellence. Operating expenses amounted to $1.3 billion, and net income was $520 million. We maintain a robust financial position with $4.8 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our outlook for the upcoming quarter is revenue of $8.0 to $8.5 billion.

I'm thrilled to dive deeper into our software and services segment, which continues to be the crown jewel of our high-margin, recurring revenue strategy. As you know, in the EV ecosystem, software isn't just a bolt-on—it's the flywheel that transforms our vehicles from depreciating assets into appreciating platforms. Today, I'll break down our Q3 performance, key drivers, regional nuances, technical milestones, and forward-looking initiatives, all grounded in the realities of a market where Tesla's Full Self-Driving beta has set the bar, Rivian's adventure subscriptions are gaining traction, and regulatory headwinds in Europe are testing everyone's mettle.

In Q3, software and services generated $1.5 billion in revenue, up a stellar 145% year-over-year and 28% quarter-over-quarter. This represents 21% of our total company revenue, a sharp rise from 9% a year ago, underscoring our pivot from hardware-heavy margins—hovering around 25% gross—to software's industry-leading 82% gross margins. For context, our remaining performance obligations for software stood at $10.2 billion at quarter-end, up 190% YoY, with 65% expected to recognize within the next 12 months. This backlog is fueled by our fleet of 3.2 million connected vehicles, which logged over 18 billion miles of real-world data in Q3 alone—more than Waymo's entire ride-hail fleet in a year.

Let's drill into the components: Subscriptions, our core growth engine, contributed $1.05 billion, or 70% of segment revenue, up 165% YoY. This includes our Apex Autonomy Suite—our Level 2+ ADAS package with highway hands-free and city-street navigation—and premium infotainment tiers like Apex Media Pro, which bundles streaming, gaming, and productivity apps. We hit 2.1 million paid subscribers, a 120% YoY increase, with an attachment rate of 45% on new vehicle deliveries, up from 28% last year. Average revenue per user climbed to $210 per month, driven by tiered pricing: Basic at $99, Pro at $199, and Ultra with predictive routing and cabin preconditioning via OTA at $299.

Autonomous driving and one-time features brought in $320 million, or 21%, including FSD-like upgrades and enterprise licensing. Our AAS Supervised v2.0, now in beta for 600,000 users, uses end-to-end neural networks trained on our proprietary Dojo-inspired supercluster, achieving 95% disengagement-free miles on highways—on par with Tesla's HW4 benchmarks. Data and services added $130 million, or 9%, from anonymized fleet data sales to insurers like predictive safety scores reducing premiums by 15% for partners like Allstate, and energy services like our V2G optimization, which monetized 3 GWh of bidirectional charging in Q3.

Trends here are unmistakable: Subscription churn dipped to 3.2% annually, best-in-class versus industry 7-10%, thanks to gamified loyalty programs and seamless OTA updates—we've pushed 15 major updates YTD, boosting feature adoption by 35%. Recurring revenue now accounts for 92% of the segment, with lifetime value per subscriber projected at $7,500 over 48 months.

On the tech front, Q3 saw the rollout of AAS v2.5, incorporating vision-only transformers with 500ms latency reductions via our custom Apex Neural Processor silicon—outperforming Nvidia Orin's TOPS efficiency by 20%. We're piloting Level 3 autonomy in select markets, with 12,000 vehicles in geo-fenced zones collecting edge-case data at 10x the rate of competitors. Our Software-Defined Everything architecture enables true OTA hardware unlocks, like retrofitting 2022 models for unsupervised city driving, unlocking $600 million in deferred revenue.

Performance varied by region: North America, 55% of segment revenue at $825 million, up 160% YoY, propelled by AAS adoption on our Zephyr and Apex platforms—U.S. take rates hit 48%, versus Tesla's ~35% FSD penetration. China, 30% at $450 million, +130% YoY despite competition from XPeng and Li Auto—our Shanghai integrations with Baidu Apollo captured 22% market share in premium subscriptions. Europe, 12% at $180 million, +90% YoY tempered by UNECE regs, but strong in Norway at 65% attachment. Rest of World, 3%, with V2G pilots in Seoul generating $25 million. Challenges like EU GDPR cap data monetization, but localized edge computing counters this.

Strategically, software is our moat—targeting $7-8 billion in full-year 2024 software revenue, implying 25-30% QoQ growth. Long-term, 40% of total revenue by 2027, with ARPU at $250 via robotaxi adjacencies—our Apex Ride-Hail beta in Austin with 60 vehicles averaging $1.20/mile gross. Investments: $500 million capex for data centers yielding 5x ROI. Risks like regulatory delays, but vertical integration de-risks.

Turning to operational metrics, as we dive into production volume and capacity utilization rates, which remain the backbone of our scaling strategy. Our team executed well, navigating supply chain headwinds and ramping key lines.

In Q3, we produced 152,400 vehicles total, a 28% YoY increase from 118,900 units, and 12% sequential from Q2's 136,000. This positions us toward full-year guidance of 580,000 to 620,000 vehicles, capturing 7.2% global share in mid-to-large SUVs per SNE Research.

By model: Zephyr SUV, 68% at 103,600 units, up 35% YoY; Apex Sedan, 22% or 33,500 units, ramping 45% sequentially; Titan Pickup, 9.5% or 14,500 units, scaling at Texas Gigafactory.

Global capacity utilization averaged 87%, up from 76% YoY and 82% QoQ—efficient for just-in-time inventory. North America at 92% on 95,000 units, Texas at 88% post-automation; Europe Berlin at 84% on 38,000 units with blade batteries; Asia-Pacific Shanghai at 81% on 19,400 units.

Initiatives: AI predictive maintenance cut downtime 15%; in-house 40 GWh prismatic cells dropped BOM 12% YoY; 95% renewable energy. Q4 production 165,000-175,000 at 90-93% utilization.

As we look at average selling price trends by model and region, ASP is a critical indicator reflecting pricing power, mix shifts, incentives, and software value. Our global ASP was $52,300 for Q3, up 8% YoY and 3% QoQ—fifth straight quarter of growth, driven by premium mix, higher FSD-equivalent attach, and battery deflation.

By model: Flagship Apex Prime sedan at $76,500, +12% YoY on 100 kWh 4680 packs and 40% autonomy attach adding $8,000; Swift crossover at $48,200, +5% YoY on AWD mix and V2H add-ons; Bolt hatchback at $35,800, -2% YoY intentional for share, offset by OTA subs.

Regionally: North America $58,400, +11% YoY on IRA credits, 92% eligible; Europe $54,100, +7% on ZEV credits and tariffs shielding; China $42,700, +4% on premium mix; RoW $49,200, +9%.

Q3 high-trim mix 62%, adding 400 bps to margins at 28.5%. Initiatives: 800V SiC inverters, solid-state pilots. Q4 ASP $53,500-$54,500.

Before Q&A, detailed forward-looking guidance on delivery volumes by model: Q3 delivered record 152,400, up 42% YoY on Shanghai ramp and US demand. Q4 guidance 155,000-165,000 total, 25-35% YoY growth, FY24 exceeding 580,000; FY25 750,000-800,000.

By model: NV-Sedan equivalent Apex Compact 28,000-32,000 Q4, China-heavy; Sport CUV 42,000-48,000, US fleets; Max Pickup 65,000-70,000, US dominant; Ultra Crossover pilots 2,000-3,000 Q4, full FY25 ramp. US 52%, China 28%, Europe/ROW 20%. Upside from FSD demos.

On gross margin per vehicle—automotive gross profit divided by deliveries: Q3 28,500 vehicles, margin $13,200 per vehicle, +18% YoY from $11,200, +5% QoQ. Automotive gross 19.8% ex-credits, ahead of Tesla peers.

YoY: COGS down 12% to $42,500 on 4680 scaling; QoQ on premium mix. Model breakdown spoken: NovaSedan-like 29% deliveries at $9,300 margin; SUV 50% at $11,700; Truck 16% at $20,200; blended $13,200. NA $14,800 on localization; Europe $10,500; APAC $9,800.

Drivers: 4680 dry electrode to $110/kWh; unboxed process 40% BIW savings; fixed cathode contracts. Q4 $13,800-$14,500.

Finally, changes in order backlog and reservation trends: Backlog $18.7 billion end-Q3, +22% YoY, 285,000 vehicles at $65,500 ASP. Flagship SUV 48%, Pickup 32%, CUV 15%. NA 62%, Europe 22%, APAC 16%. Reservations 620,000 net new 12-month, conversion 62%. Q4 backlog to $20.5-21B.

This operational leverage supports raised FY24 EBITDA to 18-20%. Next, over to Mike for manufacturing update.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Sarah. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at peak efficiency to meet growing demand. We've implemented lean principles and AI-driven maintenance, achieving 87% global utilization as Sarah detailed, with Texas and Berlin ramps ensuring scalability. We're confident in scaling further with vertical integration on cells and gigacastings.

Following me, Dr. Novak will provide insights into technological advancements.

Dr. Lena Novak:
Thank you. We continue to invest heavily in R&D to maintain our edge. Advancements in 4680 structural batteries, end-to-end neural nets for AAS v2.5, and Level 3 pilots position us as EV leaders. Our OTA roadmap and ANP silicon deliver latency reductions and hardware unlocks, fueling software growth Sarah outlined.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Analyst 1:
Thanks. Javier, on the software segment's robotaxi beta—how does Austin performance inform broader rollout, and any update on regulatory progress?

Javier Ramirez:
Great question, John. Austin's 60 vehicles are averaging $1.20 per mile gross, validating economics. Data from 18 billion fleet miles accelerates training. Regulatory-wise, NHTSA eye-off-road guidelines aid Level 3 pilots; California DMV scrutiny ongoing but de-risked by geo-fencing. Rollout to 10 cities Q4, targeting 25% ARPU uplift.

Operator:
Next question from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Analyst 2:
Sarah, with production at 152k and 87% utilization, how are you thinking about capex allocation for Texas expansion amid lithium volatility?

Sarah Chen:
Emily, capex disciplined at $500 million Q3 for data centers and ANP fabs, yielding 5x ROI. Texas adds 150k capacity YE24 via paint shop; Albemarle offtakes hedge lithium at $12k/ton. Utilization to 93% Q4 supports 165-175k without strain.

Operator:
Next from David Lee with JPMorgan.

Analyst 3:
Mike, on Berlin Gigafactory—how has blade battery integration impacted cycle times versus LFP competitors like BYD?

Mike Thompson:
David, blade integration reduced cycle times 18%, enabling LFP pivot for cost-competitive models. Utilization 84% despite regs; EU subsidies unlock €1.2B. We're at parity with BYD on efficiency, with 95% renewables aligning Scope 3.

Operator:
Next from Lisa Patel with Barclays.

Analyst 4:
Dr. Novak, AAS v2.5's vision-only transformers—can you elaborate on ANP silicon edge over Nvidia and disengagement benchmarks?

Dr. Lena Novak:
Lisa, ANP outperforms Orin by 20% TOPS efficiency, 500ms latency cut via custom photonics. 95% disengagement-free highway miles matches Tesla HW4; edge-case data from 12k Level 3 vehicles at 10x rate. OTA unlocks $600M deferred.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Operator:
Next from Robert Kim with Citi.

Analyst 5:
Javier, backlog at $18.7B—mix shift to premium and conversion rates suggest what for FY25 revenue visibility?

Javier Ramirez:
Robert, 42% backlog value from FAP and air suspension drives $65.5k ASP. NA 62% on IRA; conversion 62% lifetime. Q4 to $21B backlog supports $28B+ FY25 revenue, ramping CyberHaul-like Titan to 20% mix.

Operator:
Final question from Anna Wong with Deutsche Bank.

Analyst 6:
Sarah, gross margin per vehicle at $13,200—model breakdown shows truck strength; guidance risks from China pricing?

Sarah Chen:
Anna, VoltTruck-like Titan at $20,200 margin on gigacastings; blended +18% YoY. China ASP +4% despite wars via FOTA. Q4 $13,800-14,500 assumes 10% COGS deflation; nickel up 10% hedged, solid-state pilots de-risk.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Javier Ramirez for closing remarks.

Javier Ramirez:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are excited about the opportunities ahead—from software flywheel to production scale and premium mix—and remain committed to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to sharing our progress with you next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Apex EV Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
